title: PostMigrationCleanup verify-5b USDC skim band reverts on the very state the migration produces, bricking the finalizer (temp minter never revoked)
description: The cleanup gate's per-token 'buffer sanity band' requires `buffer = principalOf(token,original) - poolInfo(token).totalStaked` to lie in `[<token>Skimmed/2, <token>Skimmed*2]`, on the stated premise (script comment L169-180) that `buffer ≈ <token>Skimmed`. That premise is false. The buffer is dominated NOT by the leg-1 skim but by the leg-1 `initiateMigration` realize-over-credit surplus: `initiateMigration` realizes the whole old-strategy position `R` into idle balance, which exceeds the credited `P` by the strategy's accrued yield; ResetAndRewire's `setYieldStrategy` idle-sweep then folds that whole excess into V2 principal. On the real post-migration fork state the USDC buffer is 27,229,913 (~27.2 USDC) while the recorded `usdcSkimmed` is only 532,748 (~0.53 USDC) — 51.1x over the band's upper bound. The UNMODIFIED script therefore REVERTS at `Verify 5b FAILED: USDC buffer not within sanity band of usdcSkimmed`, BEFORE the sole mutation, so `phUSD.setMinter(tempStaker,false)` never runs and the migration can never be declared COMPLETE by this script as written. The DOLA pool has the same shape (~26.78 DOLA buffer) and escapes only because `dolaSkimmed==0` disables its band branch — confirming the band, not the state, is wrong.
impact: The story-060 final step is non-functional against its own correctly-migrated mainnet state. Operators running the documented runbook hit an unexplained revert at the finalizer; the temp staker retains live phUSD minter authorization indefinitely (a standing mint-capable surface the cleanup exists to remove), and 'migration COMPLETE' is never signalled. Funds are not at risk and the underlying state is solvent (principalOf > totalStaked on both pools, hard-solvency checks pass), so this is availability/operational-integrity of the finalizer, not loss — Medium.
evidence: side-effects.json unmodifiedPreview: reverted=true, revertReason 'Verify 5b FAILED…', revertedBeforeMutation=true. bandMath: usdcBufferActual 27229913 vs band [266374,1065496], ratio 51.1x. FX4 variant (band removed, hard solvency kept) passes all 12 and revokes the minter — proving the band is the sole blocker. DOLA band SKIPPED only because dolaSkimmed==0 (V4b-band postcondition result).
recommendation: Drop the `[skim/2, skim*2]` band entirely and keep only the hard solvency invariant (`principalOf >= totalStaked`, already asserted at 4b/5b) — that is the real safety property and the script's own comment admits the band is 'diagnostic-only … inexact'. If a surplus sanity bound is desired, base it on the realize-over-credit accounting (leg-1 realized `R` minus credited `P`, available from the migrator's emitted totals), not the skim alone, and log the `≈skim` comparison rather than asserting it.

title: Story-060 leaves migrator2 set on the live original staker after declaring migration COMPLETE — a standing terminal-migration footgun on a now-active pool
description: No story-060 script ever calls `original.setMigrator(address(0))` (or any reset) after leg 2. PostMigrationCleanup revokes the temp staker's phUSD minter but neither clears nor verifies the migrator. On the fork, after cleanup, `original.migrator()` and `tempStaker.migrator()` both still return migrator2 (0xd263…FFfC), an immutable `StableStakerMigrator(old=temp,new=original)`. Because `StableStaker.initiateMigration` is `onlyMigrator`, migrator2 remains an authorized path to terminally migrate the LIVE, repopulated original pool: a single owner call to `migrator2.initiateMigration(DOLA/USDC)` would freeze emissions, realize+decouple the V2 strategy, and set the pool `active=true` — which is irreversible (no resume path; staker docs: 'migration is terminal'; ledger ss9l1) and thereafter exposes a PERMISSIONLESS `userMigrate`. The intent doc's 'Post-Migration Options' section only justifies leaving the migrator set for the optional surplus re-injection and explicitly frames revocation as the expected terminal action ('do it before revoking migrator permissions'). Leaving it standing after a step whose own summary prints 'migration COMPLETE' is therefore an undocumented, non-obvious privileged surface (Law-3 footgun), not the documented option-2 state. migrator2 is also still set on the drained temp staker (harmless there, but equally never cleaned up).
impact: A non-malicious owner, believing the migration COMPLETE, retains a one-call irreversible bricking surface on a live, user-funded pool with permissionless follow-through. No unprivileged-attacker path and no fund loss absent owner action, so Low/QA — an operational hazard surfaced for safe-config, consistent with Law 3 (surprise ⇒ footgun ⇒ report).
evidence: side-effects.json preStateSummary + post-broadcast checks: original.migrator()==0xd263…FFfC and tempStaker.migrator()==0xd263…FFfC after cleanup. StableStaker.sol L148-149 onlyMigrator, L425 initiateMigration onlyMigrator nonReentrant, L555 userMigrate permissionless. StableStakerMigrator immutables old=temp/new=original (constructor L36-41). Doc 'Post-Migration Options' L224-235.
recommendation: Either (a) add `original.setMigrator(address(0))` (and on temp) as an explicit step-6 action after the verifies, or (b) if option-2 re-injection is genuinely intended, have cleanup VERIFY the migrator is the expected migrator2 and emit a loud operator instruction that revocation is still pending — and document the standing privilege in the runbook. At minimum, cleanup should assert the post-migration migrator state it is leaving behind rather than silently ignoring it.

title: PostMigrationCleanup 'verify final state' omits any SYA-wiring / V2-yield-collectability check — green-lights F3 dead-buffer config as the last gate
description: The doc bills step 6 as 'verify final state'. The script verifies V2 principal, buffer SIZE (==10) and buffer RECIPIENT on the new strategies, but never checks that the StableYieldAccumulator (SYA) / minter client was repointed to the V2 strategies or registered as a client/buffer holder on them. No story-060 script touches the SYA (cluster skipped-step b); the SYA's strategy registry and 25% buffer config still point at the OLD, post-skim-drained DOLA/USDC strategies, and the V2 strategies have only the StableStaker as a 10% client. Consequence (= deploy-entry F3 root cause): post-swap DOLA/USDC organic yield is uncollectable on the SYA side and the very 10% set-aside buffer cleanup proudly verifies (V8/V10) is dead config with no SYA consumer. Cleanup is the LAST place the suite could have caught this, and it asserts a buffer is correctly wired while not checking that anything can use it.
impact: Verification-completeness gap: the finalizer declares the end-state good while a material yield-routing leg is unwired. The economic loss (uncollectable V2 yield) is owned by F3 at the deploy entry — this finding is the missing-verification angle only, so Low/QA to avoid double-counting F3's severity. Cross-reference F3 (deploy entry) and the SYA-not-rewired cluster skipped-step.
evidence: closure-manifest cluster skipped-step 'SYA NOT REWIRED' (sharedAddresses ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2/old strategies/SYA) and sibling replace-sya (25% buffer on OLD strategies for minter+staker clients). Script L212-232 asserts setAsideBufferSize==10 / recipient==original but no SYA reference anywhere in the file. Upstream F3.
recommendation: Add a verify that the SYA (and any minter client) is a registered client on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 with the intended buffer, OR explicitly document in the runbook that SYA re-wiring is a required follow-up the cleanup deliberately does not cover and add a loud console warning. Do not assert a buffer size without asserting a consumer exists for it.

title: Story-060 fix line (vault.previewRedeem) reverts against the real Tokemak Autopool vaults — ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 deposit() is dead-on-arrival and the migration suite cannot complete
severityNote: Proposed High because this is the committed remediation for a live user-facing outage (withdrawDisabled(DOLA)==true on mainnet today) and the suite as written strands the migration after leg 1 has already moved users into the temp staker. Strict C4 mapping is Medium (failure is loud, no direct asset loss: users parked in the temp staker can withdraw since it holds funds idle) — severity-classifier to decide.
description: The story-060 fix credits `creditedPrincipal = vault.previewRedeem(sharesReceived)` inside `_acquireShares`. The intent doc prescribed `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)`. The deployment targets are NOT plain ERC4626 vaults: autoDOLA (0x79eB…A54d, 'Tokemak autoDOLA') and autoUSDC (0xa756…0D35, 'Tokemak autoUSD') are Tokemak Autopool proxies whose previewRedeem mutates state internally (withdrawal-queue simulation). Solc compiles the external `view` call as STATICCALL, so the inner state write raises StateChangeDuringStaticCall and consumes all forwarded gas: EVERY `deposit()` into the freshly deployed ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 reverts. Top-level eth_call previewRedeem succeeds (no static frame), which is exactly why off-chain checks and the committed preview JSON never caught it. Downstream, ResetAndRewire's `setYieldStrategy` idle sweep (strategy.deposit of the leg-1 skim proceeds sitting idle in the staker) and every Leg2Migration `depositFor -> _routeDeposit -> strategy.deposit` call will revert: the suite bricks at step 3/4, after leg 1 has drained the original staker into the temp staker, and the underwater-withdraw outage the suite exists to fix remains unfixed.
evidence: workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditYsSwapDeployStep1.t.sol — 3 passing fork tests against the shared anvil (block 25297374): (1) ysDolaV2-equivalent deposit of 1,000 DOLA reverts; (2) ysUsdcV2-equivalent deposit of 1,000 USDC reverts; (3) root-cause isolation — previewRedeem via contract STATICCALL reverts on both vaults while convertToAssets succeeds (autoDOLA convertToAssets(1e18)=1.16799e18, autoUSD=1086674). Trace shows revert at AutopoolETH::previewRedeem with StateChangeDuringStaticCall. side-effects.json postconditionResults[6].
impact: Migration suite cannot complete; if broadcast in order, users end up parked in the temp staker (funds recoverable via withdraw, zero emissions) with no working path back; the live DOLA withdrawal block persists. New strategy contracts are unusable as deployed.
recommendation: Change the fix to the doc-prescribed `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` (verified static-callable on both Autopools), or cache `previewRedeem` semantics via a non-view pattern. Re-deploy V2 strategies before any later leg runs. Add a deposit smoke test (e.g. a 1-wei depositAsOwner) or at minimum an in-script `try IERC4626(vault).previewRedeem(1e18)` static probe to step-1 preflight so strategy/vault incompatibility fails at deploy time, not mid-migration.

title: Leg-1 will revert at its first mutation: deployer is not an authorized withdrawer on any old strategy and no story-060 step grants it (skimSurplus is onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer)
location: SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:196-200; missing wiring belongs in DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol (step 1) or a preflight in leg 1
description: Step 2 of the suite calls `IOldYS(YS_*).skimSurplus(token, ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER)` directly from the owner-signed broadcast. `skimSurplus` is `onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer` on the deployed strategies; on live state the ONLY authorized withdrawer is the new SYA (0x3C69…8270, set by replace-sya 2026-06-10) — `authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER) == false` on all three old strategies (verified on fork). No script in the story-060 suite calls `setWithdrawer(OWNER, true)`, so leg 1 reverts at its first state-changing call.
evidence: eth_call on fork: `skimSurplus(DOLA, staker)` --from OWNER on YS_DOLA_OLD reverts with 'AYieldStrategy: unauthorized, only authorized withdrawers'. authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER)==false on 0x90ce…7F9, 0x90af…470, 0xaC2e…f95; ==true only for SYA 0x3C69…8270. grep over all 5 suite scripts: zero setWithdrawer calls. side-effects.json clusterChecks[0].
impact: Migration runbook cannot execute past step 1. Loud failure (leg-1 preview also reverts, so it would be caught pre-broadcast), but the committed suite is incomplete as written.
recommendation: Add `setWithdrawer(OWNER_ADDRESS, true)` on the three old strategies to step 1 (and revoke in PostMigrationCleanup), or route the skim through the SYA's own collection entry point. Add `require(authorizedWithdrawers(deployer))` to leg-1 preflight.

title: Post-migration yield collection silently severed: SYA still points at the old strategies and is never authorized as withdrawer on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 — staker DOLA/USDC yield becomes uncollectable and the 10% buffer is dead config
location: DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol:185-193; absence confirmed across ResetAndRewire.s.sol and PostMigrationCleanup.s.sol
description: The live yield pipeline is: strategies -> SYA.skimSurplus (SYA is the only authorized withdrawer) -> Phlimbo/NFT-minter. The new SYA (0x3C69…8270) has an on-chain strategy list [YS_DOLA_OLD, YS_USDE, YS_USDC_OLD] (read on fork) and replace-sya granted it withdrawer ONLY on those old strategies. This deploy script wires the V2 strategies' clients and buffers but never calls `setWithdrawer(SYA, true)`, and no story-060 sibling re-points the SYA (`addYieldStrategy(ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2)` / removal of the old entries) — PostMigrationCleanup only revokes the temp minter and verifies staker state. After the migration completes, all staker DOLA/USDC principal sits in V2 strategies whose surplus nothing can skim: protocol yield to Phlimbo/NFT holders from these pools silently stops, and the 10% set-aside buffer configured by this very script can never trigger (it only applies on skims). Unlike F1/F2 this failure is SILENT — nothing reverts; yield just stops flowing.
evidence: Fork reads: SYA.getYieldStrategies() == [0x90ce…7F9, 0xaC2e…f95, 0x90af…470]; ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2.authorizedWithdrawers(SYA) == false (no setWithdrawer ever called — fresh deployments, suite greps clean). side-effects.json clusterChecks[1].
impact: Permanent (until manual owner intervention) loss of yield collection for the two largest staker pools post-migration; buffer protection configured at deploy time is unreachable.
recommendation: Extend the suite (cleanup step or a dedicated rewire) to: ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2.setWithdrawer(SYA, true); SYA.addYieldStrategy(ysDolaV2, DOLA) + addYieldStrategy(ysUsdcV2, USDC); remove/retire the old strategy entries once the minter's position is resolved (see F7). Add post-conditions asserting the SYA can skim the new strategies.

title: Set-aside buffer downgraded 25% -> 10% on replacement strategies: deploy script pins the intent doc's stale figure, contradicting the user-specified 25% set by replace-sya on the live strategies two days earlier
description: The intent doc (2026-06-12) claims 'the live original staker has a 10% set-aside buffer configured' and the script hardcodes SETASIDE_BUFFER=10 with a require pinning it. But ReplaceSYAMainnet (broadcast 2026-06-10) set STAKER_BUFFER_PERCENT=25 on all three live strategies, explicitly annotated 'USER-SPECIFIED 2026-06-10: 25%' and '(live: staker 10 on USDC strategy, else 0)' — i.e. 10% was the pre-replace-sya value and 25% is the current deliberate choice. Verified on fork: old DOLA and USDC strategies both return setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25. The replacement strategies silently revert the staker's below-par insulation to 10% with no recorded rationale for the downgrade. Non-obvious owner footgun: the operator believes they are preserving existing protection ('do not carry over automatically' per the doc) while actually reducing it by 60%.
evidence: Fork reads: setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25 on 0x90ce…7F9 and 0x90af…470; ==10 on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 after this script. ReplaceSYAMainnet.s.sol:132-136 comments. Intent doc 'Set-Aside Buffer' section. side-effects.json clusterChecks[2].
impact: Stakers' set-aside reserve against below-par dips is 10% of skimmed surplus instead of the currently-chosen 25%. Moot until F3 is fixed (no skims reach the new strategies at all), which compounds the configuration debt.
recommendation: Confirm the intended buffer with the owner; if 25% stands, change SETASIDE_BUFFER to 25 and source the value from the replace-sya decision in a comment. Update the stale figure in the intent doc.

title: Replacement strategies and temp staker deployed without pauser registration — emergency pause cannot reach the contracts that will custody all staker DOLA/USDC principal
description: The live system registers global Pauser 0x7c5A…85a3 on the original staker and on all three old strategies (verified on fork). The script deploys ysDolaV2, ysUsdcV2 and the tempStaker with pauser == address(0) and neither this script nor any story-060 sibling calls setPauser. Post-migration the V2 strategies custody the staker's entire DOLA/USDC principal but are outside emergency-pause coverage; the temp staker holds all bounced principal during the leg1->leg2 window with the same gap.
evidence: Fork reads: pauser()==0x7c5A…85a3 on original staker and both old strategies; pauser()==0x0 on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2/tempStaker post-run. grep: no setPauser in the 5 suite scripts. side-effects.json clusterChecks[3].
impact: Incident response degraded for the replacement contracts (owner can still act via Ownable functions, but the pauser pathway/automation does not cover them).
recommendation: Add `setPauser(0x7c5A…85a3)` for both V2 strategies (and optionally the temp staker for the bounce window) to step 1, mirroring the old strategies' config; assert it in a post-condition.

title: Deploy script declares no post-conditions and has no resume path: 11 wiring txs under --skip-simulation can fail mid-run leaving half-wired live state, and the summary prints success regardless
description: The script's only guards are pre-flight; after 5 deployments and 11 mutations it asserts nothing (no re-read of migrator(), authorizedMinters, client/buffer state) and prints 'BROADCAST complete'. The broadcast variant runs with --skip-simulation and a Ledger: a mid-sequence failure (nonce hiccup, gas, user abort between Ledger confirmations) leaves e.g. phUSD.setMinter(temp,true) applied but migrators unset, with no idempotent re-run (re-running redeploys all five contracts, orphaning the JSON consumers' addresses). The project's own history shows this failure mode is real: story-055 required ResumeStableStakerMigration.s.sol after a mid-run failure of the previous staker migration.
evidence: Script source lines 195-239 (no requires after wiring); intent.md 'Declared post-conditions: None'; cluster evidence sibling ResumeStableStakerMigration.s.sol (story 055).
impact: Operational: partially-wired mainnet state with a stale/absent deployments JSON; recovery requires manual cast calls or a bespoke resume script under incident pressure.
recommendation: Append a _postVerify() (pattern already exists in ReplaceSYAMainnet.s.sol) re-reading every mutated slot and the five deployments before writing the JSON; consider an idempotent guard that skips deployment if a valid ys-swap-deployments.json already exists.

title: Stale NatSpec on the fixed strategy: _acquireShares doc still says principal credited is 'the full nominal amount' while the implementation credits vault.previewRedeem(sharesReceived)
location: ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:93 (@return) and 95-96 (@dev 'credits the full nominal amount (no haircut)') vs 110-113 (implementation)
description: The story-060 fix changed the credited principal from the nominal deposit amount to vault.previewRedeem(sharesReceived), but the function's @return and @dev comments still describe the pre-fix behavior. Given F1 (the fix line itself is wrong for the target vaults), this doc/code divergence is part of a pattern of the fix landing without review against its own spec.
evidence: vault@ad12cb1 source, lines cited; closure-manifest observation #1.
impact: Documentation only; misleads the next reviewer/auditor about credited-principal semantics.
recommendation: Update the NatSpec when re-fixing per F1 (the doc should then describe convertToAssets crediting and why).

title: REFERRAL (out of this entry point's slice): phUSD stable-minter retains ~13,817 DOLA + ~11,936 USDC principal on the buggy old strategies after story-060 — the over-credit bug persists for that client and the suite does not address it
severityNote: Severity provisional and tagged for referral, not direct submission from this script audit: the impact depends on phUSD-stable-minter withdrawal/accounting logic, which is outside this closure. Recommend a scoped /analyze of the minter-strategy interaction before classification.
contract: lib/phUSD-stable-minter (client position on lib/vault ERC4626YieldStrategy pre-fix builds 0x90ce…7F9 / 0x90af…470)
location: docs/stable-staker-migrations/yield-strategy-swap-June-12-2026.md 'Scope' section (staker-only); no suite script touches the minter's strategy position
description: The intent doc scopes the strategy replacement to the StableStaker client, but the underwater over-credit bug lives in the strategy contracts, which serve TWO clients. On fork: minter principal is 13,816.56 DOLA and 11,935.65 USDC on the buggy instances — roughly 13x and 6x the staker's exposure respectively. After story-060 completes, the minter keeps depositing into and accounting against strategies whose totalDeposited is systematically over-credited (the exact defect being evacuated for the staker). Whether this distorts minter redemptions/collateralization needs minter-side analysis.
evidence: Fork reads: YS_DOLA_OLD.principalOf(DOLA, minter)==13816564202291221245191; YS_USDC_OLD.principalOf(USDC, minter)==11935645684. Doc scope table. side-effects.json clusterChecks[5].
impact: The largest client of the known-buggy strategies is left on them indefinitely; accounting distortion accrues with every minter deposit into a non-1:1 vault.
recommendation: Run a scoped analysis of phUSD-stable-minter's strategy accounting; plan a follow-up migration (or strategy-side correction) for the minter's position; until then document the accepted exposure in the story-060 doc.

title: Leg1 broadcast is dead on arrival: owner is not an authorized withdrawer on any of the 3 old strategies, so the first mutating call (skimSurplus) reverts and no suite step grants the permission
location: script/SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:196-200 (skim calls), :126-138 (preflight checks owner() only); root cause lib/vault/src/AYieldStrategy.sol:461-471 (skimSurplus onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer), :224-229 (modifier), :309 (setWithdrawer, the only grant path)
description: skimSurplus is gated on the authorizedWithdrawers registry, which is fully separate from owner — the owner is never implicitly authorized. On live state the ONLY authorized withdrawer on YS_DOLA_OLD/YS_USDC_OLD/YS_USDE is the post-replace-sya SYA (0x3C690EC3B2524104dE269bf0F9baa7f045eF8270, wired by ReplaceSYAMainnet step 12 'setWithdrawer(newSYA, true)'); authorizedWithdrawers[OWNER]==false on all three (verified on fork). SkimAndLeg1Migration calls skimSurplus as the owner EOA, and neither this script nor any other story-060 step calls setWithdrawer(OWNER, true). The script's own preflight verifies owner() on all three strategies but never checks withdrawer status, so the failure is only discovered at execution. Empirically (fork preview, unmodified script, valid inputs): revert 'AYieldStrategy: unauthorized, only authorized withdrawers' at IOldYS(YS_DOLA_OLD).skimSurplus. In broadcast mode (--skip-simulation --slow) the failed skim would be a real failed mainnet tx and the suite halts at step 2 of 5. Confirms and roots upstream finding F2.
impact: The story-060 migration suite cannot execute as written: step 2 deterministically fails before any migration occurs (fail-safe — no partial state, one wasted failed tx). Migration of the buggy DOLA/USDC strategies is blocked until out-of-band setWithdrawer transactions are crafted manually.
evidence: side-effects.json executed[1] (exact revert), preconditionResults (missing check), fork reads: authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER)==false x3, authorizedWithdrawers(SYA)==true x3. Fork fixup #2 (setWithdrawer(OWNER,true) x3 from the strategies' owner) is sufficient: preview and broadcast-equivalent then complete end-to-end.
recommendation: Add to the script (inside the broadcast block, before the skims): IOldYS(ys).setWithdrawer(OWNER_ADDRESS, true) for all three strategies — the strategies' owner is the same signing EOA, so no extra signer is needed — and optionally revoke after the skims. Add a preflight require(authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER_ADDRESS)) (or perform the grant) so the script refuses to broadcast into a guaranteed failure.

title: gather-migration-inputs.js off-by-one: half-open getStakersRange treated as inclusive drops the last staker of every pool, making leg1's count preflight permanently unsatisfiable (suite DoS) with a misleading 're-run gather' remedy
location: scripts/gather-migration-inputs.js:271-284 (end = Math.min(start+PAGE_SIZE, countNum) - 1 passed as exclusive end); contract semantics lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:662-678 (getStakersRange is half-open [start,end))
description: StableStaker.getStakersRange(token, start, end) returns the half-open slice [start, end) — its NatSpec says so explicitly. The gather script computes end = min(start+200, count) - 1 and passes it as if inclusive, so every page silently loses its final element; with counts <= 200 this is exactly the last staker of each pool. Empirically on a quiescent fork (no concurrent txs possible): DOLA fetched 2 of stakerCount 3 (dropped 0x25AdA296…), USDC fetched 5 of 6 (dropped 0x0f254C40…). The script then (a) prints a WARNING attributing the mismatch to 'stakers joined between reads' and advising a re-run — which can never converge because the bug is deterministic — and (b) writes count = fetched length into leg1-stakers.json. SkimAndLeg1Migration's preflight requires that count to equal live stakerCount exactly, so leg1 (preview AND broadcast) reverts 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count in leg1-stakers.json - re-run gather' forever. Verified end-to-end on the fork. The same pager is used for --leg 2, so Leg2Migration inherits the identical block.
impact: Hard, deterministic denial of the entire story-060 migration runbook at step 2 (and again at step 4) until the JS is fixed or the input file is hand-built. Fail-safe today only by accident of double-bookkeeping: had the script written the on-chain count instead of the fetched length, the preflight would pass and the dropped staker would be silently stranded in a terminally-migrating pool (recoverable only via permissionless userMigrate or a manual migrator batch). Operator time is also burned by the actively wrong 're-run' guidance.
evidence: side-effects.json inputGathering (gathered 2/3 and 5/6 on a quiescent fork; dropped addresses identified) and executed[0] (exact preflight revert). Input fixup #1 (hand-rebuilt JSON from getStakers()) immediately unblocks the preflight.
recommendation: Use the half-open convention: const end = Math.min(start + PAGE_SIZE, countNum); pass end directly and advance start = end. Make the fetched-vs-count mismatch fatal (exit non-zero) rather than a warning, and cross-check the final list against getStakers() when count <= a sanity bound. Apply identically for leg 2.

title: Skim proceeds diverge from the migration doc: sent to the original staker instead of the treasury, leaving ~13.5 USDe orphaned as idle staker balance and ~0.15 USDC + ~2.9 USDe parked on the phUSD minter via the old strategies' per-client buffer routing
location: script/SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:196-201 vs docs/stable-staker-migrations/yield-strategy-swap-June-12-2026.md:133-135, 224-234; buffer routing: deployed pre-story-025 bytecode at the 3 strategies (no setAsideBufferRecipient — selector reverts on-chain; pinned ad12cb1 source routes the aggregate buffer to setAsideBufferRecipient instead)
description: The intent doc's step 1a skims all three strategies to 'treasuryAddress' and its Post-Migration Options section reasons about surplus 'sitting at the treasury address as raw tokens'. The script instead skims to ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER, relying (per its post-assert comment) on ResetAndRewire's setYieldStrategy sweep to fold the idle balance into the V2 strategies as a principal buffer. That plan only covers DOLA and USDC: the USDe pool is never re-wired, so the USDe proceeds observed on the fork (+12.31 USDe recipient share + ~1.19 USDe staker buffer share = ~13.49 USDe) sit as unreserved idle balance on the staker indefinitely — reachable only via a manual StableStaker.rescueERC20 (StableStaker.sol:808) that no suite step performs. Additionally, the DEPLOYED old-strategy bytecode routes each client's 25% set-aside buffer to the client contract itself (observed: 0.152660 USDC and 2.916739 USDe transferred to the phUSD minter 0x435B0A18…), a behavior that differs from the pinned ad12cb1 source and is mentioned nowhere in story-060. All flows are protocol-owned (no user funds at risk) but the doc's accounting of where surplus ends up is wrong on three counts.
impact: Protocol-owned value scattered across unintended resting places: ~13.5 USDe orphaned on the staker (manual rescue required, undocumented), ~$3 equivalent on the phUSD minter contract. Doc-driven follow-ups (e.g. 'option 2: re-inject from treasury') would target an address holding nothing. Operationally non-obvious — a competent operator following the doc would be surprised (Law-3 footgun, low value at current scale).
evidence: side-effects.json stateWrites (USDe/USDC balance deltas incl. minter receipts), unintendedEffects, on-fork probe: setAsideBufferRecipient() selector reverts on deployed strategies while setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25.
recommendation: Update the migration doc to match the implemented destination and sweep plan; add an explicit step (cleanup script is the natural place) that rescueERC20s the idle USDe to the intended treasury; document the minter-side buffer receipts or zero the buffers before skimming.

title: Staleness guard is count-equality only: equal-count membership drift between gather and broadcast passes preflight, strands the unlisted staker in a terminally-migrating pool, and the script is not re-runnable (initiateMigration is one-shot)
description: The preflight compares only .count against live stakerCount. If one staker exits and another enters between the gather snapshot and the broadcast (counts equal, membership different), preflight passes; batchMigrate then processes the stale list — the departed address yields amount 0 (skipped) and the new staker is never migrated. The post-assert stakerCount==0 does catch it, but in broadcast mode (--skip-simulation --slow) it fires only AFTER all on-chain txs have landed: both pools are then in terminal Migrating state with one stranded staker, and simply re-running the script reverts at initiateMigration (already migrating; the staker contract blocks re-engagement). Recovery is possible but undocumented: the stranded user can self-rescue via permissionless userMigrate, or the owner can run a manual migrator1.migrate(token,[missed]) — neither appears in the runbook. The exposure window is short (stake/withdraw freeze once initiateMigration lands, so only gather → initiateMigration), but this repo has prior history of exactly this snapshot-vs-broadcast drift biting on this staker slice (story-055 ResumeStableStakerMigration). With the current 3/6-staker population the probability is low; the cost is an aborted mainnet run mid-suite.
impact: Operational footgun: a benign user action in the gather→broadcast window can leave the migration half-finished on mainnet with no scripted recovery path. No funds lost (userMigrate exists); availability/runbook risk only.
evidence: Code reading of preflight + StableStaker terminal-migration semantics; story-055 resume script as prior drift evidence (closure manifest cluster note). Not fork-demonstrated (would require staged user txs); flagged as analysis-supported.
recommendation: Strengthen the guard: have gather also store keccak256 of the sorted staker list and have preflight recompute it from getStakers() on-chain; or migrate from a fresh on-chain getStakers() read inside the script instead of a JSON snapshot (counts are tiny). Document the userMigrate/manual-batch recovery in the runbook.

title: viem is not declared in package.json: the mandatory gather prerequisite cannot run from a clean checkout
description: gather-migration-inputs.js requires viem and exits with 'viem not installed. Run `npm install` in the project root first.' — but viem is absent from both dependencies and devDependencies, so npm install does not provide it and the suggested remedy fails, mirroring LEG1-02's misleading-guidance pattern. The operator must know to npm install viem manually. Since leg1 hard-depends on the gather output (preflight reads leg1-stakers.json), this is a setup blocker on any fresh machine — exactly the environment a Ledger-signing mainnet operation is likely to run from.
impact: Runbook friction/blocker only; no on-chain effect.
evidence: side-effects.json inputGathering.viemDependency; package.json deps block verified at b27c6ac.
recommendation: Add viem (pinned) to package.json dependencies.

title: Leg2 re-deposit silently haircuts each user's principal by ~0.026% (DOLA) / ~0.016% (USDC); intent doc states principal is preserved 1:1
description: migrator2.migrate -> depositFor -> _routeDeposit deposits each migrating user's snapshot credit into the FIXED V2 ERC4626YieldStrategy, which (per story-060's own fix) credits convertToAssets(sharesReceived) rather than the nominal amount. The integer-rounding shortfall (received - credited) stays protocol-owned in the strategy, so each user's withdrawable principal on the original staker is strictly less than what they held on the temp staker. Measured on-fork: every DOLA position lost ~0.0260-0.0262% and every USDC position lost ~0.0157-0.0158% (e.g. 0x4B75.. DOLA 1018.123 -> 1017.858, -0.265 DOLA). The story-060 intent doc (User Impact) states 'Principal is preserved 1:1 (subject to any below-par haircut from the old buggy strategy)' — it discloses the OLD-strategy (R,P) haircut but NOT this fresh re-deposit haircut introduced by the leg2 deposit into the new strategy.
impact: Real, permanent per-user principal reduction (small, uniform, proportional). Not a 1:1 round-trip as documented. Because tempStaker holds principal idle (no strategy), leg1's deposit was lossless, so this is a SINGLE fresh ERC4626 haircut, not a compounded one — but it is undisclosed value leakage from the user's perspective and accrues to the protocol/strategy buffer.
evidence: side-effects.json perUserValuePreservation: DOLA total before 1033.6189 -> after 1033.3501 (loss 0.2688 DOLA, 0.0260%); USDC total before 1954.5707 -> after 1954.2630 (loss 0.3077 USDC, 0.0157%). yieldStrategy(DOLA)==yieldStrategy(USDC)==address(0) on temp confirms leg1 was lossless. The shortfall is the conservative-rounding behaviour the fix intends (consistent with the underwater-guard design) — it is the DOC that overstates preservation.
recommendation: Update the story-060 intent doc User Impact section to disclose that the leg2 re-deposit into the new ERC4626 strategy applies a small (~0.02-0.03%) conservative convertToAssets haircut to each position, distinct from the old-strategy (R,P) socialization. No code change required — the haircut is the correct, conservative accounting; only the 1:1-preservation claim is inaccurate.

title: gather-migration-inputs.js --leg 2 drops the last staker of each pool (LEG1-02); halts leg2 at the count-equality preflight rather than silently partial-migrating
description: LEG1-02 (already filed for leg1) applies IDENTICALLY to migrate:ys-swap-gather-leg2 against the temp staker. The loop computes end = Math.min(start+PAGE_SIZE, countNum) - 1 and passes it as the EXCLUSIVE end of the on-chain half-open getStakersRange(token,start,end), so the final staker per pool is never fetched. Confirmed on-fork: gather wrote count=2 (DOLA) and count=5 (USDC), dropping 0x25AdA296.. (DOLA) and 0x0f254C40.. (USDC). The gather only emits a NON-FATAL console.log WARNING ('fetched 2 stakers but stakerCount returned 3'), which an operator running under automation could miss. NOTE: this is a duplicate root cause of LEG1-02 — recorded here only to document its leg2 reachability and the downstream fail-safe; do not double-count severity.
impact: If the operator does not notice the WARNING and runs leg2 with the raw gather output, Leg2Migration's _globalPreflight count-equality guard (leg2DolaCount == tempStaker.stakerCount(DOLA)) reverts with 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count - re-run gather' (verified on-fork). So LEG1-02 cannot cause a silent partial migration via leg2 — it causes a hard, fail-loud halt. The residual risk is operational friction + a dropped staker being temporarily stranded on temp until the operator regenerates the input. Without the workaround the dropped stakers (0x25Ad.. / 0x0f25..) would remain on tempStaker after leg2 with no automated path back.
evidence: side-effects.json gatherResult + unmodifiedPreview (revert reason 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count in leg2-stakers.json - re-run gather', 2 != 3). leg2-stakers.BUGGY-LEG1-02.json captured. Fixed by regenerating from getStakers() full membership (3/6).
recommendation: Fix the gather loop (pass count as the exclusive end, or use getStakers()), and/or make the count-mismatch WARNING a hard process.exit(2) so the gatherer cannot emit an under-count file. The on-chain preflight is a good last line of defense and should be kept.

title: Leg2 broadcast is non-idempotent: a halted/partial broadcast leaves temp pools in terminal Migrating state and re-running the documented command reverts at initiateMigration with no resume path
description: The broadcast variant uses --skip-simulation (a deliberate response to the story-055 RESUME stale-calldata incident). If the broadcast halts after Step 1 (initiateMigration(DOLA)/(USDC)) but before all migrate chunks land — RPC drop, gas spike, manual Ctrl-C, or a chunk reverting — the temp pools are left in PoolState.Migrating. Re-running the SAME documented command (`migrate:ys-swap-leg2`) reverts immediately at the first action, because StableStaker.initiateMigration requires poolState == Active ('StableStaker: pool not active'). Unlike the project's resilient progress.<chainId>.json deploy scripts, Leg2Migration has no checkpoint/skip-completed logic and no resume mode: it always tries initiateMigration first. There is also no in-script guard that detects an already-Migrating pool and jumps straight to the migrate loop.
impact: Operational halt footgun. A non-malicious operator who sees a half-completed broadcast will reach for the obvious recovery (re-run the script) and hit a confusing revert. Recovery requires out-of-band action: calling migrator2.migrate(token, remainingChunks) directly for the not-yet-migrated stakers (or affected users self-rescuing via userMigrate). Funds are not lost (idle pile + snapshot credit are intact and migrate is replay-safe per-user since _exitPosition skips zeroed positions), but the system is left half-configured and the documented runbook command cannot finish it. Same failure class as story-055 ResumeStableStakerMigration, which existed precisely to repair this.
evidence: StableStaker.sol:initiateMigration require(poolState==Active) (verified). Leg2Migration.s.sol always calls initiateMigration before the migrate loops with no Active/Migrating branch. The migrate loop itself IS idempotent (batchMigrate skips amount==0 positions), so a resume path is feasible — it just isn't implemented.
recommendation: Add a resume-aware branch in run(): before Step 1, read tempStaker.poolState(DOLA/USDC); if already Migrating, skip initiateMigration for that token and proceed directly to the migrate chunk loop (which is replay-safe). Optionally persist a tiny progress marker consistent with this repo's progress.<chainId>.json convention so a half-completed leg2 can be finished by re-running the documented command instead of ad-hoc cast calls.

title: Leg2 preflight guards staleness only by staker-count equality, not set membership; a same-count membership change between gather and broadcast slips the drift guard
description: The only freshness guard on leg2-stakers.json is leg2{Dola,Usdc}Count == tempStaker.stakerCount(token). This catches additions and removals that change the count but NOT a count-preserving membership swap. Between the gather snapshot and the in-script Step-1 initiateMigration the temp pools are still Active, so a user can stake into temp and another can withdraw to zero (net count unchanged), changing the set while preserving the count. The gathered chunk would then migrate a now-exited address (no-op, _exitPosition returns 0, skipped) while NOT migrating the new joiner (absent from the chunk).
impact: Low and largely self-fail-safing. The new joiner is left on temp, so the post-assert tempStaker.stakerCount(token) == 0 FAILS and the run reverts (fail-loud) — no silent loss. Residual risk is the operational halt + a brief window where a same-count swap is possible (requires a withdraw-to-zero and a fresh stake within the gather->broadcast window, on a transit staker most users never interact with directly). The set-membership exposure is narrower for leg2 than a general staker because temp is a short-lived transit contract, but the guard is weaker than it could be.
evidence: Leg2Migration.s.sol:126-136 (count-only require). StableStaker stake/withdraw permitted while Active (poolState gating). closure-manifest cluster note flags the same count-equality-only weakness for gather staleness.
recommendation: Strengthen the guard: either (a) hash the gathered staker set and compare against an on-chain enumeration in preflight, or (b) since temp is transit-only, freeze it before gather (e.g. set phUSDPerDay to 0 and socially/technically prevent new stakes), or (c) run gather immediately before broadcast and rely on the existing post-assert as the backstop (current de-facto practice). Document the gather->broadcast window as a no-new-stakes operational window.

title: ResetAndRewire broadcasts with --skip-simulation and a non-idempotent step sequence: the F1 deposit revert lands mid-suite on mainnet, leaving pools Active/strategyless/unpaused with no re-run path through the entry point
description: The broadcast entry uses `--skip-simulation --slow`, so forge sends txs one-by-one without a pre-broadcast bundle simulation. With the strategies as actually deployed (upstream F1: ERC4626YieldStrategy._acquireShares line 113 calls Tokemak previewRedeem, which mutates state and reverts under STATICCALL — empirically reconfirmed here: the unmodified fork preview reverts with StateChangeDuringStaticCall at the FIRST setYieldStrategy), the mainnet run executes tx1 finalizeAndReset(DOLA) and tx2 finalizeAndReset(USDC) successfully and then halts at tx3 setYieldStrategy(DOLA, ysDolaV2) with an on-chain reverted transaction. The resulting halt state: both pools revived to Active with yieldStrategy == address(0), migrator still migrator1, idle 26.785 DOLA + 27.234 USDC unswept on the staker, and 9 users (1033.6 DOLA + 1954.57 USDC) parked yield-less in the temp staker. The entry point is NOT re-runnable after fixing the strategies: finalizeAndReset requires PoolState.Migrating, so tx1 reverts on every retry ('pool not migrating') — and with --skip-simulation each retry burns another reverted mainnet tx before the operator learns this. Worse, the halt window is publicly exposed: neither staker is paused (verified paused()==false) and stake() on an Active strategyless pool succeeds (idle-hold path), so ANY deposit — innocent or a 1-wei grief (ledger ss10l1) — sets totalStaked > 0 and re-locks setYieldStrategy behind the story-010 empty-pool gate, forcing a full second terminal-migration cycle just to wire replacement strategies. A default forge simulation (no --skip-simulation) would have simulated the 6-tx bundle, hit the tx3 revert, and refused to send ANYTHING — zero on-chain damage; the flag converts a free preflight catch into a half-configured mainnet system.
impact: Protocol availability + operational hazard, no direct fund loss: migration suite halts half-configured on mainnet; user principal stranded (recoverable) in the temp staker until a manual out-of-runbook recovery (cherry-picked setYieldStrategy/setMigrator calls with fixed strategies); recovery itself griefable via the story-010 gate during the unpaused halt window. The brick root cause is F1 (deploy entry — referenced, not duplicated); THIS finding is the script-level amplification: skip-simulation + non-idempotent ordering + unpaused halt window.
evidence: side-effects.json `unmodifiedPreview` (revert at tx3 with tx1/tx2 succeeding, unmodified-preview.log); StableStaker.finalizeAndReset require(poolState==Migrating) (lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:594); paused()==false on both stakers at post-state; story-010 gate at StableStaker.setYieldStrategy:228; forge zero-damage alternative verified by the default-simulation semantics of forge script.
recommendation: 1) Drop --skip-simulation from all ys-swap broadcast entries (the suite's value of it is unclear; Ledger signing does not require it). 2) Make the script resumable: guard each step (skip finalizeAndReset when poolState is already Active; skip setMigrator when already set) so a halted run can be re-broadcast. 3) Pause both stakers for the migration window (stake is whenNotPaused; finalizeAndReset/setYieldStrategy are deliberately pause-tolerant) to close the public-stake gate-relock during any halt. 4) Run the preview variant against live mainnet immediately before broadcast as a hard runbook gate — the preview demonstrably catches F1.

title: Preflight wires JSON-sourced strategy addresses and grants them unlimited token approval without any on-chain identity verification (code presence, vault, underlying, client authorization)
description: _globalPreflight checks only that ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 are non-zero in script/migration-inputs/ys-swap-deployments.json. It never verifies on-chain that (a) the addresses have code, (b) strategy.vault() is the expected autoDOLA/autoUSDC, (c) strategy.underlyingToken() matches the pool token, or (d) strategy.authorizedClients(ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER) == true — the doc's own 'Wire' checklist item ('setClient ... needed for leg 2 re-deposit') that, if missed in step 1, makes tx3 revert AccessDenied mid-suite with exactly the half-configured halt shape of SCRIPT-RESET-01. setYieldStrategy also grants the address an UNLIMITED token approval before the first compatibility check executes. The risk of address drift in this file is not hypothetical: the closure manifest documents a preview-derived address (0x190cBd59...) colliding with live foreign mainnet code, and the deployments JSON is a mutable build artifact rewritten by step 1.
impact: Law-3 non-obvious footgun / weak drift guard. A stale, preview-contaminated, or mis-wired deployments JSON passes preflight and either halts the suite mid-broadcast (revert in the sweep deposit) or, if the foreign address tolerates the calls, leaves a max-allowance to an unvetted contract wired as the pool's strategy. No direct loss demonstrated; all observed fork values were correct.
evidence: side-effects.json preconditionResults (only non-zero checks present); doc yield-strategy-swap-June-12-2026.md 'Wire' checklist; closure-manifest.json unresolved[1] (0x190cBd... collision); cast verification this audit had to do manually (vault()/underlyingToken()/authorizedClients all checked out on the fork).
recommendation: Add to _globalPreflight, per strategy: require(addr.code.length > 0); require(IYS(addr).vault() == EXPECTED_VAULT && IYS(addr).underlyingToken() == token); require(IYS(addr).authorizedClients(ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER), 'setClient missing - run step 1 wiring'). Constants for the two expected vault addresses already exist in the doc.

title: PREVIEW_MODE env leakage silently turns the broadcast entry into a no-op that still patches mainnet-addresses.ts (empirically: zero-tx 'broadcast' exits 0, so the && chain runs the patcher)
description: Mode selection is an environment variable, not a CLI fact: if PREVIEW_MODE=true is still exported in the operator's shell (highly plausible — the documented runbook has the operator run the *-preview entries, and an `export PREVIEW_MODE=true` while iterating leaks into the broadcast invocation), `npm run migrate:ys-swap-reset` runs forge with --broadcast but the script takes the vm.startPrank branch, records ZERO broadcastable transactions, and — empirically verified on the fork with a minimal probe — forge prints only 'Warning: No transactions to broadcast' and EXITS 0. The && chain then runs patch-mainnet-addresses-ys-swap.js, which unconditionally rewrites YieldStrategyDola/YieldStrategyUSDC in server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts. Result: the address registry (consumed by the UI/API per server architecture) now claims the V2 strategies are live while on mainnet the pools are still Migrating with no strategies wired and migrator1 in place. Nothing in the on-chain state stops a later leg2 attempt from failing confusingly, and the only console hint is a '*** PREVIEW MODE ***' log line mid-scroll.
impact: Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun: off-chain deployment registry desyncs from mainnet with exit-code success, misleading the UI and the operator's runbook checkpointing. No funds at risk directly; the on-chain system is simply not migrated.
evidence: Empirical probe (script taking the prank branch under --broadcast): forge exit code 0 with 'Warning: No transactions to broadcast'; patch script has no on-chain verification (scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-ys-swap.js trusts ys-swap-deployments.json only); ResetAndRewire.s.sol:174 envOr default false.
recommendation: Make the broadcast entry pin the env: `PREVIEW_MODE=false forge script ...` in package.json (one-word fix), and/or have the script require consistency: in broadcast mode `require(!vm.envOr("PREVIEW_MODE", false), "PREVIEW_MODE set on broadcast entry")` is impossible as written (the flag IS the mode switch), so instead derive mode from forge context (vm.isContext(ForgeContext.ScriptBroadcast)) rather than an env var. Additionally, the patcher could verify on-chain (eth_call: original.yieldStrategy(DOLA) == ysDolaV2) before rewriting the registry.

title: Intent-doc / NatSpec / code three-way disagreement on the expected post-wire principal (doc: ==0; script header: >0; code: two-sided bound) — doc lag from the skim-parking decision
location: doc 'Step 3' (Verify: principalOf == 0 expected); ResetAndRewire.s.sol:23-27 (header: principalOf > 0); ResetAndRewire.s.sol:231-239 (code: principalOf <= idleSwept && (idleSwept==0 || principalOf>0))
description: The intent doc instructs the operator to verify `YieldStrategyDolaV2.principalOf(DOLA, originalStableStaker) == 0 (expected — pool was empty before wiring)`, written before the design decision (leg1, commit 71c545c lineage) to PARK the skim surplus as idle balance on the staker and let setYieldStrategy fold it into the V2 strategies as an unattributed principal buffer. The script's own NatSpec header says the opposite (`principalOf > 0 (set-aside buffer deposited by staker)`), and the code implements a third, correct, two-sided variant. Empirically the code is right (principal 26.778 DOLA / 27.229 USDC <= swept 26.785 / 27.234, both > 0) — but an operator cross-checking against the doc's '== 0' during a live mainnet broadcast would conclude the migration mis-fired. Also minor: the doc splits 'Step 3 reset' and 'Step 4 wire migrator2' while the script merges both into one broadcast (benign, but runbook step numbering no longer matches script numbering).
impact: Law-2 faithfulness / QA: stale runbook verification values can cause a false alarm (or worse, train the operator to ignore verification mismatches) during a live migration. No on-chain impact; the coded asserts supersede the doc and passed on the fork.
evidence: side-effects.json postconditionResults; doc lines under 'Step 3 — Reset original and wire new strategies'; script NatSpec lines 23-27 vs code lines 231-239.
recommendation: Update the doc's Step-3 verification to the swept-idle bound (principalOf <= idle swept, > 0 when idle was non-zero) and renumber the doc steps to match the merged script; align the script header comment with its own code.
